4→
5→## The important ones
6→
7→| Codeword | Plain meaning |
8→|---|---|
9→| **Fleet driver** | The product: one orchestrator agent that directs Claude/Codex/GLM coding tools, sends them work, watches them, and interrupts/steers them. Formerly also called the "Conductor." |
10→| **Conductor** | Same as fleet driver. (Being phased out.) |
11→| **Referee** | The feature that re-runs a worker's tests itself instead of trusting the worker's "it passed." It's how the driver knows "done" is real. **Not** a separate product — a trust feature of the driver. |
12→| **Worker / harness** | A full coding tool (Codex, Claude Code, or GLM) doing a task, running in its own copy of the repo. |
13→| **Orchestrator** | The boss that decides what to do — your CLI agent (Claude Code or Codex). |
14→| **The hub / coordinator** | The reliable program underneath the orchestrator that carries out its decisions and does bookkeeping. |
15→| **Adapter** | The piece of code that translates the driver's commands into a specific tool's real API (one adapter per Codex/Claude/GLM). |
16→
17→## Framing terms (mostly retired)
18→
19→| Codeword | Plain meaning |
20→|---|---|
21→| **The moat** | The hard-to-copy advantage. |
22→| **Data flywheel** | The saved history of past runs that makes routing smarter over time. |
23→| **Neutral trust institution** | A framing that was **retired** (doc 19) — it wasn't the goal. Ignore it. |
24→| **Rental vs. moat** | Parts a better AI model will make pointless (rental) vs. parts that stay valuable (moat). |
25→| **Subtractive thesis** | "Cut features; give the agent less, not more." |
26→| **Bitter lesson** | The observation that general methods + bigger models tend to beat hand-built cleverness — so don't over-engineer scaffolding a better model will route around. |
27→

29→
30→| Codeword | Plain meaning |
31→|---|---|
32→| **Northbound / southbound** | Toward the orchestrator (up) / toward the workers (down). |
33→| **Control plane / data plane / knowledge plane** | The interrupt-and-steer channel / the message channel / the shared memory. |
34→| **Capability plane** | The tools the driver hands its workers (search, debug, etc.). |
35→| **Stigmergy / stigmergic** | Workers coordinate by reading and writing shared files/notes, instead of messaging each other directly. |
36→| **Blackboard** | A shared scratchpad workers read and write. |
37→| **MCP** | A standard way for an AI agent to call tools; how the orchestrator talks to the driver. |
38→| **ACP** | A standard for one program to drive an AI coding tool; a fallback way to reach workers. |
39→
40→## Reliability rules (the "I" numbers — engineering shorthand)
41→
42→These live inside the supervisor spec and are fine there, but shouldn't appear in plain prose without their gloss:
43→
44→| Codeword | Plain meaning |
45→|---|---|
46→| **Fencing / I1** | Version-stamp every command so a stale one (aimed at what the worker *was* doing) is rejected. |
47→| **At-least-once cursors / I3** | Track "what has the reader seen" so a crash never silently drops events. |
48→| **Two-phase stop / I6** | Don't call a worker "stopped" until it actually confirms it stopped. |
49→| **Hub-run verification / I7** | Re-run the worker's check yourself before believing "done." (= the "Referee.") |
50→| **Single-consumer approval** | A worker's question/approval is answered exactly once, even if two people could answer. |
51→
52→## Tool / analysis words
53→
54→| Codeword | Plain meaning |
55→|---|---|
56→| **Representation ladder / AST / CPG / IR / e-graph** | Ways to look at code as *structure* instead of raw text, so you can tell a real change from a reformat. |
57→| **Semantic diff** | A diff that shows what *behavior* changed, hiding renames and reformatting. |
58→| **Three-tempo memory** | Fast (live scratchpad) / medium (task list) / slow (long-term knowledge) memory. |
59→| **Validation / Evidence ladder** | Levels of checking, cheap to expensive: types → tests → property tests → fuzzing → math proof. Use the cheap rung unless the task needs more. |
60→| **Autoformalization** | Turning an English spec into a math-checkable statement — the hard, unsolved part of proving code correct. |
61→
62→## Experiment names
63→
64→| Codeword | Plain meaning |
65→|---|---|
66→| **E1** | The experiment "does a team of AIs beat one good AI?" (expensive to test). |
67→| **E2** | The cheaper experiment "does a different-vendor check catch bugs the same vendor misses?" — optional de-risking of the re-verification feature, **not** a decision on whether to build the driver. |
68→| **Pass@N** | The chance at least one of N tries succeeds. |
69→
